excerpts.text: The spacecraft was built by Ball Aerospace and was launched by SpaceX on a Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California.

## Launch

SPHEREx was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at the Vandenberg Space Force Base, California on March 11, 2025. The launch was procured by NASA's Launch Services Program and was conducted as a shared mission with the Polarimeter to UNify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) spacecraft.

* August 03, 2022: NASA confirmed that SPHEREx will launch alongside the PUNCH (Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere) mission as a secondary rideshare payload. This decision optimizes launch costs and aligns with mission requirements. 13)

excerpts.text: | Launch date | 12 March 2025, 03:10:00 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC "UTC") (11 March 2025, 8:10 pm [PDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time "Pacific Time"))[[1]](#cite_note-launch-date-1) |

**Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere** (**PUNCH**), also known as **SMEX-15**, is a mission by [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") to study the unexplored region from the middle of the [solar corona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_corona "Solar corona") out to 1 [AU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astronomical_unit "Astronomical unit") from the [Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun "Sun"). The PUNCH flight assets are a constellation of four [microsatellites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Small_satellite "Small satellite") that through continuous 3D deep-field imaging, will observe the corona and [heliosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heliosphere "Heliosphere") as elements of a single, connected system. The four microsatellites were initially scheduled to be launched in October 2023, but were moved to launch alongside ([rideshare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rideshare_payload "Rideshare payload")) the [SPHEREx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SPHEREx "SPHEREx") space observatory on a Falcon 9 Block 5 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base, from which all five satellites were successfully deployed on 11 March 2025.[[3]](#cite_note-nasa-20220803-3)[[1]](#cite_note-launch-date-1)[[4]](#cite_note-4)
